chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Malik ibn 'Atiyyah, from Fulan ibn 'Ammar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The registers on the Day of Judgment are three: a register containing blessings, a register containing good deeds, and a register containing sins. The register of blessings is juxtaposed with the register of good deeds, so the majority of the good deeds are consumed [to offset the blessings], and the sins remain.

key_terms.يُقَابَلُ: Juxtaposed or offset against each other

ai.seo_question: What happens to good deeds on the Day of Judgment according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the mechanics of divine justice by describing three registers: blessings, good deeds, and sins. In this Shia theological framework, the vast majority of one's good deeds are consumed to repay the countless favors (ni'am) God bestowed, leaving the sins to be weighed against the remaining balance, highlighting the necessity of abundant worship to offset divine favors.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 10.Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Mālik ibn ʿAṭiyyah, from Fulān[1] ibn ʿAmmār who said,

“Abū ʿAbdillāh (a) said, ‘The registers on the Day of Judgment will be three: A register in which the blessings are listed, the register in which is the [record of one’s] good deeds, and the register in which will be the [record of] sins. Then the register of blessings will be juxtaposed with the register of good deeds, so all the good deeds will be taken up [as what was due for the blessings that were granted], and [only] sins will remain.’”
